Skat Rules

Skat after the official rules: three players, 32 cards, bidding, the skat and the game value.

The rules

Cards and deal
32 cards, 7 to Ace. Each player gets 10, two go face down into the skat. Points: Ace 11, Ten 10, King 4, Queen 3, Jack 2, Nine, Eight and Seven 0 - 120 in all. The player after the dealer is Forehand, the next Middlehand, the dealer Rearhand.
Bidding
Middlehand bids to Forehand: 18, 20, 22, 23, 24, 27, 30 and so on - only values a game can have. Forehand holds or passes. The one left over is then bid to by Rearhand. Whoever is left is the declarer. If nobody bids, Forehand may still play for 18; otherwise the deal is passed in.
Skat or Hand
The declarer takes the skat and puts any two cards away (their points count for the declarer), or plays Hand without looking at it. Only in a Hand game can Schneider, Schwarz or Ouvert be announced.
The games
Suit game (Clubs 12, Spades 11, Hearts 10, Diamonds 9): the four Jacks and the chosen suit are trumps. Grand (24): only the four Jacks are trumps. Null (23, Hand 35, Ouvert 46, Ouvert Hand 59): no trumps, and the declarer must not take a single trick.
Order of the cards
Trumps: Jack of Clubs, Jack of Spades, Jack of Hearts, Jack of Diamonds, then Ace, Ten, King, Queen, Nine, Eight, Seven of the trump suit. Other suits: Ace, Ten, King, Queen, Nine, Eight, Seven. In Null: Ace, King, Queen, Jack, Ten, Nine, Eight, Seven.
Following suit
Forehand leads the first trick, then the winner of each trick leads. You must follow the suit led (the Jacks belong to the trumps); if you cannot, you may play any card.
Winning
The declarer wins with 61 points or more. Schneider: one side has 30 points or less. Schwarz: one side takes no trick. If Schneider was announced the declarer needs 90 points, if Schwarz was announced every trick.
Game value
Base value times the level. The level is the matadors ("with" or "without" so many top trumps, counted from the Jack of Clubs, skat included) plus 1 for the game, plus 1 each for Hand, Schneider, Schneider announced, Schwarz, Schwarz announced and Ouvert. Null games have fixed values.
Lost and overbid
A lost game counts double against the declarer. If the value is lower than the bid, the game is overbid and lost; it counts the lowest multiple of the base value that reaches the bid, doubled.
The score list
After each game the declarer gets the value (won) or minus twice the value (lost). The list adds up all games; a passed-in deal is noted with no points.
French and German cards
Under New game you can choose French cards (Clubs, Spades, Hearts, Diamonds) or German cards (Acorns, Leaves, Hearts, Bells). In German cards the Ober takes the place of the Queen and the Unter that of the Jack (U), the rules stay the same.

Counting the matadors

Clubs, and the declarer holds the Jack of Clubs and the Jack of Spades but not the Jack of Hearts: "with 2, game 3", so the value is 3 x 12 = 36.
